title: How Real World Goblins Actually Works
description:
A plain explanation of the mechanics behind Real World Goblins, an NFT/token project built on Robinhood Chain -- based on the project's own published documentation.

This is not financial advice, and it's not an endorsement -- it's a mechanical explainer. For transparency: the creator of this video holds Real World Goblins NFTs and RWG tokens.

#web3 #nft #cryptoexplainer

scenes.text: Real World Goblins is a new project on a chain called Robinhood Chain, built around a fantasy NFT collection with real financial mechanics underneath it.
Each Goblin NFT gets its own smart contract wallet, called an ERC 6551 account, so it can hold and manage its own assets on chain.
How many Goblins ever exist depends on how many whitelist spots get reserved by burning for them before September the eleventh, at eleven eleven AM Eastern.
Minting itself is free. Once minted, a Goblin can be exchanged for one million RWG tokens at a marketplace called the Grotto, which charges a variable fee based on RWG's price.
Goblins can equip items bought with a token called GG. The very first item is the Enchanted Doll, which actually gets consumed to mint a Goblin.
Trading fees from three different sources get shared with Goblin holders who join something called the Horde, as long as their Goblin has a financial item equipped.
You can also lock GG for a token called xGG, or stake different liquidity pairs, to earn a share of ongoing GG and RWG rewards.
A portion of the protocol's fees get converted into a separate token called GLD. Eighty percent of those fees go to one randomly chosen Goblin, every single week.
There's also a lending system. You can borrow against a locked Goblin or against items, but items get liquidated once the loan reaches seventy percent of their value.
The rest of the roadmap includes the RWG token launching on Uniswap, Goblins actually being minted, and the Grotto, Bazaar, and Counting House opening up over time.
That's how the mechanics work as of today. This isn't financial advice, and for full transparency, I hold Goblin NFTs and RWG tokens myself.
